cover.headline: Claude now reads *24 months* of your bank history. *Read-only.*
cover.sub: Five launches from 5 to 7 Nov and the fences around them, plus two free courses.

items.title: Claude can read your bank. It can't *move money*
items.statLabel: months of transactions it reads, across up to 16 US banks
items.what: Anthropic's Personal Finance beta links accounts through Plaid for US Pro, Max and Ultra users. Read-only, and off in Claude Code.
items.why: An assistant now sees the same feed as a budgeting app. Insight stops being the moat; what you are licensed to do with the money is.

items.title: GPT-6 Cyber ships *invite-only*
items.statLabel: per million output tokens, for approved Daybreak Red orgs
items.what: Rated Critical for cybersecurity. Orgs need SSO, MFA and IP allowlisting. Individuals also need a physical FIDO2 key.
items.why: Copy the access model for your own strong AI tools: verified identity, hardware keys and allowlisted networks first.

items.title: DeepMind's agents found two cracks in *1024-bit RSA*
items.statLabel: cheaper to factor each extra 1024-bit key in a batch
items.what: Agents guided by cryptanalysts also found a signature forgery about 1,600x better than the old best, in theory. RSA-2048 is untouched.
items.why: 1024-bit keys still hide in old HSMs, VPN boxes, firmware and internal PKI. Inventory them this week and set retirement dates.

items.title: Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash: *15-second* clips, 30% cheaper
items.statLabel: list price of one 15-second 720p clip at $0.07 a second
items.what: Generally available on Google Cloud since 6 Nov. Clips run up to 15 seconds, up from 10, with an invisible SynthID watermark.
items.why: A 15-second ad variant now costs about a dollar to draft. The real cost moves to human review and the media behind the winners.

items.title: Microsoft runs a coding agent *on one GPU*
items.statLabel: GB of GPU memory runs Qwen3.8-27B behind GitHub Copilot
items.what: Foundry Local serves a 4-bit Qwen3.8-27B, about 18 GB, to Copilot via bring-your-own-key. Microsoft says code never leaves the machine.
items.why: Code that can't leave the building gets an agent without a cloud exception. Expect weaker reasoning than frontier models.

courses.title: MCP Security Fundamentals
courses.note: freeCodeCamp, about 2 hours, posted 29 Oct. Break the lethal trifecta with architecture, not prompt filters.

courses.title: Learn Vector Databases for Beginners
courses.note: freeCodeCamp, 1.5 hours, posted 3 Nov. Embeddings, HNSW and IVF indexes, then a ChromaDB search build.

read: Claude reads your bank but can't move *a cent*. GPT-6 Cyber needs *hardware keys*. Microsoft's coding agent never leaves the laptop. Pick the fence before the model.
takeaway: Write the permissions first: what the AI reads, what it can do, where it runs.
